value:
THE RUN-30 WORK ORDER'S PREMISE -- 'the ~55-site bidirectional live-zero population has NO PROOF MODE' -- IS REFUTED ON TWO INDEPENDENT GROUNDS, AND THE STRONGER PROOF MODE'S PAYOFF SET IS MEASURED EXHAUSTED. Zero score movement; this is a REFUTED/RECLASSIFIED deliverable, not a dead end. It bounds claim.CV_residual-family-census.20260901.v1, whose 56/55 direction split is correct as a MEASUREMENT of the residual population but which was read as a statement about tool coverage, and it is consistent with (not a correction to) claim.law.WF_inverse-copy-form-is-served-and-the-payoff-inversion-recurs-one-level-down.20260901.v1.

GROUND 1 -- THE MODE ALREADY EXISTED WHEN THE WORK ORDER WAS WRITTEN, in both arrows and at both levels of the stage stack. `equivalent_copy_form` accepts `dominating_def_inverse` and `dominating_def_inverse_across_calls` (ours is the copy, the target the `li`; shipped in commit 7eb8cd0b9, 'Match fn_8001267C via inverse copy-form direction'), and the COMBINED form+recolor stage accepts `unconditional_recolor`, `constant_dataflow_recolor` and `constant_dataflow_inverse_recolor` (commit 02ba94ae5). The work claim was recorded at 21:30Z; those commits and the WF law describing them predate it. A lane ordered to BUILD this would have rebuilt a shipped mechanism.

GROUND 2 -- THE NEWEST AND STRICTLY STRONGEST MODE HAS AN EMPTY UNSERVED PAYOFF SET, MEASURED IMAGE-WIDE. verify_value_equality_recolor landed at 2026-09-01 18:36Z, AFTER the CH census (15:37Z, claim.law.CH_census-screen-2-excludes-the-zero-impure-population...) had screened this population with the strictly weaker strict-renaming proof. That gap is a genuine, concrete lead and it was executed rather than assumed: all 93 equal-size paired functions whose every differing word is register-field-only were re-screened under BOTH proofs, with the declarations harvested from the shipped verifier's own refusal messages, never hand-written. RESULT: strict recolor passes 70; value-equality closes 72; the difference is exactly TWO, and BOTH are already shipped -- game/game/controls::InitControls (pinned, closed by the earlier WF lane at 19:21Z per attempt.WF_initcontrols-value-equality-close.20260901.v1) and game/pb/dbgtext::fn_800C031C (pinned since 2026-08). The stronger mode buys ZERO functions that are not already served.

THIS IS AN INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION, WHICH IS THE POINT. The earlier WF lane reported 'one of only 2 hits among 91 pure register-field candidates across 2842 equal-size functions, and the other hit was an already-pinned canary'. This pass, written from scratch with a different candidate filter and a different declaration harvester, found 93 candidates and the SAME 2 hits with the SAME canary. Two independent censuses agreeing to the function is much stronger evidence of exhaustion than either alone.

A METHOD TRAP THAT COST A FALSE NEGATIVE HERE, worth more than the headline. The first run of the ledger reported 0 new closers, because its refusal parser handled only the per-site message ('+0xNN: use of gA is not value-equal to gB') and not the AGGREGATE one the verifier emits when it wants several escapes declared at once ('undeclared value-equality substitution(s): +0xNN gA->gB, ...'). Both hits refuse through the aggregate form, so a screener that parses only the per-site form declares the whole population empty and looks entirely plausible doing it. ANY auto-declaring screen must handle EVERY refusal shape the verifier can emit, and must be validated against a known-closable canary before its negative result is believed -- a canary is what turned this from a false all-clear into the correct answer.

THE STANDING LEDGER, which is the reusable artifact. Of the 23 register-field-only functions that neither proof closes, 13 are PINNED (already served; they appear only because the scan reads raw bodies) and 8 are GENUINELY OPEN, each with a named site and cause: five are the permanently-unforcible 'base register presence differs (g0 vs gNN)' class -- critter::CritterLoadDone +0x98, critter::CritterLoadStartNext +0xe0, gamemain::fn_80054E78 +0x154, psfx::LoadPdataFile +0x118, attract::scroll_credits +0xe4 -- which REPRODUCES CH's list EXACTLY, same five functions, same five offsets, a second independent corroboration. The remaining three are genuine value inequalities: movieplayer::fn_800DBE98 +0x3c (f0 vs f2), tower::towerRecordLevelBeaten +0x20 (g30 vs g31), memcard::drawMemCardMessage +0x84 (g26 vs g22). The first two are 2 of CH's 4 'inconsistent renaming' refusals and are now DECIDED under the stronger proof rather than merely unscreened; CH's other two have since been served (InitControls closed, TowerCheckMessages pinned). drawMemCardMessage is new to this ledger.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TRIAGE: do not commission another live-zero or value-equality proof-mode build, and do not re-screen the register-field-only population -- cite this record. The next honest capability question in this family is the COMPOSED one (permute evaluated AFTER the form rewrite), which claim.law.DC_copy-form-class-is-directional-and-its-inverse-population-is-unserved.20260901.v1 already specifies and which this pass did not touch.
